A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PLUS study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v2 reports original reward-model experiments on Pets, UltraFeedback, and PRISM, including ablations, generalization tests, and GPT-4 personalization results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds larger-model ICL evaluations and additional training trajectories.

M1.justification: The stated PRISM summarizer instructions change from generic preference extraction under 50 words to explicit guidance about verbosity, diversity, and fluency under 100 words (v2 Appendix I.1; v3 Appendix J.1). The co-adaptation algorithm, model architecture, and losses remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Pets, Pets OOD, UltraFeedback-P2/P4, and PRISM, including flexible user contexts and held-out conversations/users. The larger ICL models extend configurations within existing coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator methods remain BTL, DPL, VPL, ICL, PLUS-untrained, and the oracle, with the existing GPT-4 comparisons retained. The added 7B/8B evaluations use the same ICL method.

E3.justification: v3 Appendix B adds ICL evaluations using Llama8B-Instruct and Qwen7B-Instruct on UltraFeedback-P2/P4. The documented PRISM summarization prompt also changes its guidance and word limit. These revisions do not establish that the retained PRISM results were rerun.

E4.justification: The larger-model ICL comparison tests whether increased model capacity closes the gap to PLUS. v3 Figure 3 adds Pets and UltraFeedback-P2 training trajectories and replaces the PRISM traces. Existing co-adaptation ablations, OOD tests, and qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: Tables 1–2 switch from standard deviations to two-sided 95% t-intervals over three seeds. Table 1 also changes UF-P4/Qwen0.5B from single-seed entries to three-seed summaries. Other three-seed counts remain unchanged, and Table 2 inconsistently retains the old 'mean and std' wording.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises UF-P4/Qwen0.5B results, including PLUS from 61.8 for one seed to a three-seed mean of 62.10. New Table 6 reports ICL accuracies of 61.4/58.6 for Llama8B and 61.8/58.8 for Qwen7B on UF-P2/P4. Training trajectories also change; the PRISM benchmark scores and GPT-4 win rates remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix A's mathematical compression example is removed: it defines rewards above and below y=x and contrasts an informative angular representation with z'=theta1, which cannot recover the reward. This removes a small expressivity argument; the main definitions and Equations 1–6 are retained.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain co-adaptive textual user summaries, improved personalized reward prediction, topic-shift robustness, flexible inputs, and GPT-4 personalization. Replacing 'zero-shot' with 'without further fine-tuning' clarifies a procedure already stated in v2; the headline claims remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 adds specific limitations concerning PPO hyperparameter sensitivity, instability, and under-convergence, with prospective mitigation strategies. It also expands privacy considerations for maintaining user information. Poor PRISM generalization to unseen users was already discussed in v2's appendix and is now highlighted in the main text.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-access link and reproducibility statement, specifies implementation sources more precisely, and adds batch-size and epoch observations. It revises the PRISM prompt and describes 2–4 H200 GPUs instead of four, while removing v2's explicit LoRA fine-tuning disclosure.

R1.justification: The LoRA reference by Edward J. Hu et al. (2021) is removed with its implementation citation. The related-work discussion and positioning against embedding-based personalization and prior summarization work otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes the presentation: numbered experimental subsections become compact run-in headings, the discussion is condensed and expanded with limitations, and ethics/reproducibility statements are added. Motivation moves into Section 4, response examples move to the appendix, and the appendix organization is reworked.

P2.justification: v3 adopts the ICLR title, header, and typography format; changes Figure 1's vignette; removes the compression diagram; and replaces the training plots with a three-dataset figure. The unstructured-input table gains a condensed main-text display while its full version moves to the appendix, alongside a new larger-model table and relocated examples.

improvement.justification: Larger ICL controls and broader three-seed uncertainty reporting modestly strengthen the empirical evidence. Added training limitations and code-access information improve transparency. These gains outweigh localized reporting regressions, including conflicting uncertainty wording in Table 2 and removal of the explicit LoRA detail; the core method and PRISM conclusions remain largely unchanged.
